docs.title: Disqt VPS Wiki
docs.text: Welcome to the documentation for the disqt.com VPS infrastructure. This wiki covers all services running on the server, including game servers, APIs, monitoring, and supporting infrastructure.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The disqt.com infrastructure runs on a Debian VPS hosted on OVH. It hosts game servers, web APIs, a Discord bot, and a full metrics monitoring stack.

docs.title: Service Overview
docs.text: Service Port User Protocol Public Path CS2 Server 27015 cs UDP Direct connect Minecraft PaperMC 25565 minecraft TCP Direct connect Xonotic 26420 xonotic UDP Direct connect Discord Bot - cs - - lgsm-info-api 8080 dev HTTP /servers miaro-scheduler-api 8081 dev HTTP /miaro Website - - HTTP / Node Exporter 9100 root HTTP localhost only Process Exporter 9256 root HTTP localhost only Prometheus 9090 dev HTTP localhost only Grafana 3000 dev HTTP /metrics nginx 80/443 root HTTP/S Reverse proxy

docs.text:
Internet

nginx (80/443)

docs.title: Key Design Decisions
docs.text:
• SSH access is on port 24420 (not the default 22).
  • User isolation: Each service runs under its own Linux user (cs, minecraft, xonotic, dev). See Users & Access for details.
  • No Docker: All services run natively as systemd units, or via screen/tmux for game servers.
  • nginx serves as the single entry point for all HTTP traffic, handling SSL termination and reverse proxying to backends.

docs.title: Game Servers
docs.text: The VPS hosts three game servers, each running under its own dedicated Linux user.

docs.title: Connection Details
docs.text: Game Address Port Counter-Strike 2 disqt.com 27015 Minecraft disqt.com 25565 (default) Xonotic disqt.com 26420

docs.title: Server Pages
docs.text:
• CS2 Dedicated Server -- Counter-Strike 2 with custom plugins, modes, and bot management
  • Minecraft Server -- PaperMC with AuthMe, BlueMap, and automated backups
  • Xonotic Server -- Deathmatch with grappling hook, managed by LinuxGSM

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
Connect via the CS2 console or Steam server browser:

connect disqt.com:27015

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• User: cs
  • Game files: /home/cs/cs2/
  • Plugin framework: CounterStrikeSharp (.NET 8.0), installed via Metamod
  • Console: screen -r cs2 (detach with Ctrl+A, D)

docs.title: Server Control
docs.text:
/home/cs/start-cs2.sh    # Start the server
/home/cs/stop-cs2.sh     # Stop the server
screen -r cs2             # Attach to the server console

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text:
File Purpose /home/cs/cs2/game/csgo/cfg/server.cfg Base server settings /home/cs/cs2/game/csgo/cfg/bots.cfg Bot behavior and quotas /home/cs/cs2/game/csgo/cfg/ffa.cfg, comp.cfg, etc. Mode-specific overrides

Warning

Mode configs can override server.cfg settings. If a CVar change is not persisting, check the active mode's cfg file.

docs.title: Bot CVars Reference
docs.text:
bot_quota 0                    # Don't auto-fill bots
bot_quota_mode "normal"        # Don't auto-add to quota
bot_join_after_player 0        # Don't auto-join when human joins
mp_autoteambalance 0           # Allow unbalanced teams
mp_limitteams 0                # No team size limits
bot_difficulty 5               # 1=pacifist, 2=easy, 3=normal, 4=hard, 5=expert

docs.title: Building and Deploying DisqtModes
docs.text:
cd /home/cs/disqt-bot/DisqtModes && dotnet build -c Release
cp bin/Release/net8.0/DisqtModes.dll \
  /home/cs/cs2/game/csgo/addons/counterstrikesharp/plugins/DisqtModes/
cp -r lang \
  /home/cs/cs2/game/csgo/addons/counterstrikesharp/plugins/DisqtModes/

After deploying, restart the server for changes to take effect.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
CounterStrikeSharp logs are located at:

/home/cs/cs2/game/csgo/addons/counterstrikesharp/logs/

docs.title: bot_add Sometimes Adds Extra Bots
docs.text:
Running !bot add 1 occasionally adds 2 bots instead of 1. Investigated mitigations (all applied but the issue persists):

  • bot_join_after_player 0 in bots.cfg
  • bot_quota 0 with bot_quota_mode "normal"
  • mp_autoteambalance 0 and mp_limitteams 0

Possible remaining causes include game mode configs resetting bot CVars during mode transitions, or CS2 engine behavior with the bot_add command.

docs.title: Warmup Duration Overrides
docs.text: mp_warmuptime 10 is set in server.cfg, but some game modes override this value in their own cfg files.

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
Connect using the default Minecraft port:

disqt.com

Port 25565 is the Minecraft default, so no port specification is needed.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Server software: PaperMC
  • Mode: Offline mode with AuthMe for authentication
  • User: minecraft
  • Management: LinuxGSM (/home/minecraft/pmcserver)

docs.title: Server Control
docs.text:
/home/minecraft/pmcserver start      # Start the server
/home/minecraft/pmcserver stop       # Stop the server
/home/minecraft/pmcserver restart    # Restart the server
/home/minecraft/pmcserver console    # Attach to the console

docs.title: Member Management
docs.text:
Player access is managed through a combination of:

  • Whitelist: Controls who can join the server
  • AuthMe: Handles player authentication (required since the server runs in offline mode)
  • LuckPerms: Permission groups for role-based access control

docs.title: BlueMap
docs.text:
A 3D world viewer is available at disqt.com/map. BlueMap renders the Minecraft world as an interactive 3D map accessible from any browser.

Use the /bmdiscover command in-game to trigger 3D model generation for newly explored areas.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text: Plugin Purpose AuthMe Player authentication (offline mode) LuckPerms Permission groups and roles BlueMap 3D world viewer at disqt.com/map WorldEdit In-game world editing Multiverse-Core Multi-world management AxGraves Player graves on death SkinsRestorer Custom skins (offline mode support) Chunky Pre-generation and world border spark Performance profiling and monitoring

docs.title: Configuration Hierarchy
docs.text:
LinuxGSM uses a layered configuration system:

_default.cfg < common.cfg < pmcserver.cfg

Settings in pmcserver.cfg override common.cfg, which overrides _default.cfg. Only put custom settings in pmcserver.cfg.

docs.title: Automated Tasks (Crontab)
docs.text: Task Schedule Description Monitor Every 5 minutes Checks if the server is running, restarts if crashed Update Saturday 4:00 AM Updates PaperMC to the latest build LinuxGSM Update Saturday 5:00 AM Updates LinuxGSM itself Backup Daily 6:00 AM Creates a backup of the world and config

docs.title: Discord Alerts
docs.text: Server events (crashes, restarts, updates) are sent to the alert-minecraft Discord channel.

docs.title: Map Management
docs.text:
• MCASelector: Used for selective world resets (delete specific region files)
  • BlueMap /bmdiscover: Triggers 3D model generation for newly loaded chunks

docs.title: Known Issue: Invisible Walls
docs.text:
If players experience invisible walls, this is a client-side version mismatch, not a server issue.

Fix: Ensure the client Xonotic version matches the server version, and clear the download cache:

~/.xonotic/data/dlcache/

Delete the contents of this directory and reconnect.

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text: The disqt.com VPS is a Debian server hosted on OVH. This section covers the underlying infrastructure that supports all services.

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
• User isolation: Each service runs under its own Linux user for security and separation of concerns.
  • systemd services: Most long-running processes are managed as systemd units.
  • nginx reverse proxy: All HTTP traffic enters through nginx, which routes requests to the appropriate backend.
  • SSH on port 24420: SSH access uses a non-standard port for basic security hardening.

docs.title: Infrastructure Pages
docs.text:
• nginx -- Reverse proxy configuration and routing
  • Metrics Monitoring -- Prometheus, Grafana, and exporters
  • systemd Services -- Service units and management commands
  • Users & Access -- Linux users and SSH configuration
  • Kernel Tuning -- Network optimizations for game servers

docs.title: Network Optimizations
docs.text:
Network buffer sizes and queue depths are tuned for game server traffic in /etc/sysctl.d/99-gameserver.conf:

net.core.rmem_max = 4194304
net.core.wmem_max = 4194304
net.core.rmem_default = 1048576
net.core.wmem_default = 1048576
net.core.netdev_max_backlog = 5000

docs.title: What These Do
docs.text:
• rmem_max / wmem_max: Raises the maximum UDP receive/send buffer to 4MB (default was 208KB). This prevents packet drops under high game server load.
  • rmem_default / wmem_default: Sets the default buffer to 1MB so new sockets start with a reasonable size.
  • netdev_max_backlog: Increases the network backlog queue to 5000 packets, preventing drops during traffic spikes.

These settings benefit all game servers (CS2, Minecraft, Xonotic) running on the VPS.

docs.title: Applying Changes
docs.text:
sudo sysctl --system

This reloads all sysctl configuration files, including the game server tuning.

docs.title: CS2-Specific CVars
docs.text:
These CVars are set in server.cfg to complement the kernel tuning:

sv_maxrate 0                    # Unlimited bandwidth per client
sv_minrate 128000               # Minimum 128KB/s per client
sv_parallel_sendsnapshot 1      # Multi-threaded snapshot sending
sv_clockcorrection_msecs 15     # Tighter clock sync (competitive standard)

Invalid CSGO-era CVars

These CVars do not exist in CS2 (Source 2 engine). Using them produces "Unknown command" errors in the server console:

  • net_splitpacket_maxrate
  • net_splitrate
  • net_maxcleartime
  • sv_pure

docs.title: Tick Rate
docs.text: CS2 runs at 64 tick with sub-tick input timestamping. This is hardcoded by Valve and cannot be changed through server configuration.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The Grafana dashboard is available at disqt.com/metrics.

  • Public access: Read-only dashboards are available without login.
  • Admin access: Login required for editing dashboards and configuring data sources.

docs.title: Stack
docs.text:
Component Version Port Purpose Node Exporter 1.10.2 9100 System metrics (CPU, RAM, disk, network) Process Exporter 0.8.7 9256 Per-process CPU and memory metrics Prometheus 3.9.1 9090 Scrapes exporters, stores time series data Grafana 12.3.2 3000 Dashboards and visualization

All components are installed as native binaries (no Docker).

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
Exporters (9100, 9256)  -->  Prometheus (9090)  -->  Grafana (3000)  -->  nginx  -->  Browser
                              (15s scrape)            (dashboards)       (/metrics/)
  • Prometheus scrapes exporters every 15 seconds.
  • Data retention is 30 days.
  • All components bind to localhost only; Grafana is exposed through the nginx reverse proxy at /metrics/.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
/home/dev/metrics/
  bin/                          # node_exporter, process-exporter, prometheus, promtool
  prometheus/prometheus.yml     # Scrape configuration
  prometheus/data/              # Time series storage (30-day retention)
  process-exporter/config.yml   # Process name matchers
  grafana/                      # Grafana data (database, provisioning)
  grafana-dist/                 # Grafana distribution (binaries + assets)
  grafana.ini                   # Grafana configuration

docs.title: Tracked Processes
docs.text:
The Process Exporter monitors the following services:

Process Match Method CS2 comm: cs2 Minecraft cmdline: .*paper\.jar.* Xonotic cmdline: .*xonotic.* Discord bot cmdline: .*bot\.py.* lgsm-info-api cmdline: .*lgsm-info-api.* miaro-scheduler-api cmdline: .*miaro.* nginx comm: nginx Prometheus comm: prometheus Grafana comm: grafana

Note

comm matches the binary name (first 15 characters of /proc/PID/comm). cmdline uses regex against the full command line. When both are specified, both must match (AND logic).

docs.title: Service Management
docs.text:
All monitoring components run as systemd services:

sudo systemctl restart node-exporter
sudo systemctl restart process-exporter
sudo systemctl restart prometheus
sudo systemctl restart grafana

docs.title: nginx
docs.text: nginx serves as the reverse proxy for all HTTP traffic on the VPS.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The main site configuration is located at:

/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/disqt.com

docs.title: Routing Table
docs.text: Path Backend Notes / Static files disqt-info-website /servers localhost:8080 Cached 10min, stale-while-revalidate /miaro localhost:8081 miaro-scheduler-api /metrics/ localhost:3000 Grafana dashboards /map/ BlueMap Minecraft 3D map

docs.title: SSL/TLS
docs.text: HTTPS is provided by Let's Encrypt certificates, managed by certbot. Certificates are automatically renewed.

docs.title: Common Commands
docs.text:
sudo nginx -t          # Test configuration for syntax errors
sudo nginx -s reload   # Reload configuration without downtime

Always run nginx -t before reloading to catch configuration errors.

docs.title: systemd Services
docs.text: Most long-running services on the VPS are managed as systemd units.

docs.title: Service Units
docs.text: Unit Name User Description disqt-bot.service cs Discord bot lgsm-info-api.service dev Game server status API miaro-scheduler-api.service dev Work schedule API node-exporter.service root System metrics exporter process-exporter.service root Per-process metrics exporter prometheus.service dev Metrics aggregation grafana.service dev Metrics dashboards

docs.title: Common Commands
docs.text:
sudo systemctl status <unit>      # Check service status
sudo systemctl restart <unit>     # Restart a service
sudo systemctl stop <unit>        # Stop a service
sudo systemctl start <unit>       # Start a service
sudo journalctl -u <unit> -f      # Follow live logs
sudo journalctl -u <unit> --since "1 hour ago"  # Recent logs

Note

Minecraft and Xonotic use LinuxGSM (not systemd) for server management. CS2 uses manual start/stop scripts with screen. See their respective pages for control commands:

  • CS2
  • Minecraft
  • Xonotic

docs.title: Linux User Isolation
docs.text:
Each service runs under its own dedicated Linux user for isolation and security:

User Purpose Home Directory cs CS2 server + Discord bot /home/cs/ minecraft Minecraft PaperMC server /home/minecraft/ xonotic Xonotic server /home/xonotic/ dev APIs + metrics monitoring /home/dev/

docs.title: SSH Access
docs.text:
• Port: 24420 (not the default 22)
  • All service users have passwordless sudo for administrative tasks.

docs.title: Services
docs.text: The VPS runs several supporting services alongside the game servers.

docs.title: Service Directory
docs.text: Service Repository Description Discord Bot disqt-discord-bot CS2 server control via Discord Server Status API lgsm-info-api Game server status JSON endpoint Scheduler API miaro-scheduler-api Work schedule tracker Website disqt-info-website Server status dashboard

docs.title: Service Pages
docs.text:
• Discord Bot -- Python bot for controlling the CS2 server via Discord slash commands
  • lgsm-info-api -- Go API that queries game servers and returns their status as JSON
  • miaro-scheduler-api -- Go API for a 10-day rotating work schedule
  • Website -- Static dashboard displaying live game server status

docs.title: Discord Bot
docs.text:
• Repository: disqt-discord-bot
  • Runtime: Python (discord.py)
  • User: cs
  • Location: /home/cs/disqt-bot/
  • systemd unit: disqt-bot.service

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Discord bot provides remote control of the CS2 server through Discord slash commands. It communicates with the CS2 server using the Source RCON protocol.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description /cs exec <cmd> Execute an RCON command /cs map <name> Change map (supports Workshop URLs) /cs maps List available maps /cs competitive Switch to Competitive mode /cs arena Arena mode /cs gungame Arms Race mode /cs retake Retake mode /cs ffa FFA Deathmatch /cs sandbox Practice mode /cs status Show server status and player list /cs bot add [n] Add bots /cs bot kick Kick all bots /cs bot difficulty <level> Set bot difficulty

docs.title: Access Control
docs.text: Commands are restricted to users with a configured Discord role. Only members with the appropriate role can interact with the bot.

docs.title: Bot Presence
docs.text: The bot updates its Discord presence every 30 seconds, displaying the current map and player count on the CS2 server.

docs.title: Multi-Language Support
docs.text: The bot supports French and English. Language files are stored as JSON in the lang/ directory.

docs.title: DisqtModes Plugin
docs.text: The bot repository also bundles the DisqtModes CounterStrikeSharp plugin (C#), which adds in-game modifiers, bot management, and workshop map support. See the CS2 page for details on DisqtModes.

docs.title: Service Management
docs.text:
sudo systemctl restart disqt-bot    # Restart the bot
sudo systemctl status disqt-bot     # Check status
sudo journalctl -u disqt-bot -f     # Follow logs

docs.title: lgsm-info-api
docs.text:
• Repository: lgsm-info-api
  • Runtime: Go (Gin framework)
  • Port: 8080
  • User: dev
  • systemd unit: lgsm-info-api.service

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A lightweight HTTP API that queries all game servers and returns their status as JSON. It uses the external gamedig CLI tool to probe each server.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
GET /servers

Returns a JSON array with the status of each game server:

  • Server name
  • Running status
  • Current player count
  • Maximum players
  • Connect URL

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
nginx caches the /servers endpoint with a 10-minute TTL and stale-while-revalidate. This means:

  • Responses are served from cache for up to 10 minutes
  • When the cache expires, nginx serves the stale response while fetching a fresh one in the background
  • This reduces load on the game servers and ensures fast response times

docs.title: Consumer
docs.text: The response is consumed by the Disqt website at disqt.com/servers to display live server status on the dashboard.

docs.title: Service Management
docs.text:
sudo systemctl restart lgsm-info-api    # Restart the API
sudo systemctl status lgsm-info-api     # Check status
sudo journalctl -u lgsm-info-api -f     # Follow logs

docs.title: miaro-scheduler-api
docs.text:
• Repository: miaro-scheduler-api
  • Runtime: Go (Gin framework)
  • Port: 8081
  • User: dev
  • systemd unit: miaro-scheduler-api.service

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A 10-day rotating work schedule tracker. The API calculates the current shift based on a fixed cycle that started on August 31, 2024.

docs.title: Schedule Pattern
docs.text:
The 10-day cycle repeats continuously:

Days Shift Hours 0-1 Morning 06:00 - 14:00 2-3 Afternoon 14:00 - 22:00 4-5 Night 22:00 - 06:00 6-9 Free -

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Endpoint Description GET /health Health check GET /miaro HTML dashboard with current schedule GET /miaro/json JSON response with schedule data

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• Timezone: Europe/Paris
  • Cycle start: August 31, 2024

docs.title: Access
docs.text: The dashboard is accessible at disqt.com/miaro.

docs.title: Service Management
docs.text:
sudo systemctl restart miaro-scheduler-api    # Restart the API
sudo systemctl status miaro-scheduler-api     # Check status
sudo journalctl -u miaro-scheduler-api -f     # Follow logs

docs.title: Disqt Website
docs.text:
• Repository: disqt-info-website
  • URL: disqt.com

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A static HTML/JS/CSS dashboard that displays the live status of all game servers. The site features a neon/cyberpunk visual theme.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Real-time status: Fetches server data from the /servers API endpoint (provided by lgsm-info-api)
  • Player counts: Shows current and maximum players for each server
  • Click-to-copy: Server addresses can be copied to clipboard with a single click

docs.title: Hosting
docs.text: The website is served directly by nginx as static files. There is no build step required -- the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files are served as-is.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: Update the static files on the server and nginx will serve the new version immediately. No restart is needed.
